grade_reason: The only statements found since 1 January 2025 are about AI education and small-business use of AI, with no acknowledgment of catastrophic risk. His earlier work on extreme AI risks dates from 2024, before the search window.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. IMPORTANT for the reviewer, outside the window: on 16 April 2024 Moran joined Sens. Romney, Reed and King in a framework for federal oversight of frontier AI aimed at biological, chemical, nuclear and cyber threats (https://www.reed.senate.gov/news/releases/romney-reed-moran-king-unveil-framework-to-mitigate-extreme-ai-risks); search summaries say a bill version followed with Sen. Hassan, described by the group ARI as addressing existential risks (https://ari.us/senators-intro-bipartisan-ai-bill-to-mitigate-existential-risks/, not opened). Moran's own quote in the April 2024 release frames AI as an opportunity. I found no evidence that this bill was reintroduced since January 2025, but I did not check congress.gov. No source shows him co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (reported as a Sanders and Casar bill). A States Newsroom article of 30 June 2025 (https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/changes-made-ai-moratorium-amid-bills-vote-rama) says Moran was expected to vote against the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws; this is a report, not a quote, and I did not verify his vote, so it is left out of the record. Pages I could not open: cantechletter.com article of January 2025 on his AI risk management bills (blocked), askapol.com 2024 interview (not found). His press release index shows only the 10 most recent releases, so older 2025 to 2026 releases were not browsed page by page. Rep. Nathaniel Moran of Texas (AI Kill Switch Act) appears in many results and is a different person; nothing of his is attributed here. The two quotes were retrieved through a page-reading tool that returns extracted text, so a reviewer should confirm the exact wording on the pages.
